newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U2 to play in Sarajevo in September.
newsitem.headline: U2 to play in Sarajevo in September.

text.p: The Irish rock group U2 will play for Bosnians in Sarajevo this year, the band's manager Paul McGuinness announced on Wednesday.
As a part of its "Pop Mart" world tour which starts in Las Vegas in April, the band will play in Sarajevo on September 23 after its Italian and Austrian performances.

Donating the proceeds of the concert to rebuilding of a war-damaged medical centre in a western Sarajevo suburb, McGuinness said the band was privileged and honoured to play in the once besieged city.
"The appalling things that happened to this city over the past few years are known to us but perhaps not as well known around the world as they should be," he told reporters.
The band's outspoken singer Bono has paid a private visit to Sarajevo and celebrated a first post-war 1995/96 New Year's eve in the city, saying there was no better place in the world for it.
He often used U2 concerts to attack Western powers for failing to end the war in Bosnia during the 3 1/2 years of fighting.
The city's biggest stadium Kosevo can take up to 40,000 people but many more are expected to see the spectacle from the surrounding hills, a city official Amira Kapetanovic said.
The band's 200 support staff and 50 equipment trucks promise a spectacle unseen in Sarajevo since Elton John played in 1983.
Kapetanovic said it was possible that Italian tenor Luciano Pavarotti would join U2 at the Sarajevo concert because he will be opening a music centre in the southern town of Mostar in September.
